newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand's resurgence continued unchecked on Tuesday as the tide of exporter and offshore dollars continued to flow into the local currency market.
At the 1400 GMT local close, the rand had firmed another two cents to 4.5625/5675 against the dollar from 4.5825/5855 on Monday, bringing its gains to 14 cents so far this year.

The currency began the day faced with an overhang of dollars out of New York overnight. That, as well as continued local exporter dollar selling helped the currency to a day's strongest level of 4.5620 bid by noon.
Dealers said that at that level the rand ran into profit-taking and some importer demand carried it back to close to 4.58, where sellers re-emerged.

"We saw some dollars coming back in above 4.57 out of London after profit-taking and a bit of importer demand at 4.5620," a dealer said, adding that the currency appeared well offered at the 4.58 level.
Dealers said that the rand's close away from the 4.58 level was technically a bullish factor.
Boyde Stafne, technical analyst at UAL Merchant Bank, said he was cautiously bullish about the currency's short-term prospects.
"I think that the key hinges on two levels. Below 4.58 I am cautiously bullish. Below 4.55 I will probably change that to outright bullish," Stafne said.
"I haven't quite seen 4.55 yet, but so far it is looking pretty good...a little overbought but looking good," he added.
The rand also continued to gain ground against the crosses, firming to 7.3370/3553 against sterling from 7.3570/3574 on Monday and to 0.3613/3623 marks from 0.3570/3574 previously.
On the capital market, bonds had an indifferent day as the market shrugged off a slightly better-than-expected December inflation number and small bouts of profit-taking set in.
The key R150 was last quoted at a 15.45 percent yield compared with 15.39 percent on Monday.
"It's been quite an interesting day. For the first time we have seen a bit of foreign selling and some profit-taking," a dealer said. "Overall though its been pretty lacklustre."
The dealer said while the December CPI data had beaten market expectations -- rising 9.4 percent year-on-year compared with forecasts of a 9.6 percent rise -- reactions were relatively muted.
Direction on Wednesday was expected to be provided by latest money supply data, due for release after the market closed.
On the money market, Reserve Bank figures showed liquidity eased further on Monday as the shortage eased to 9.842 billion rand from to 9.999 billion rand on Saturday.
Three-month NCD rates were steady at between 17.10 and 17.25 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was slightly lower at between 16.40 to 16.60 percent from 16.45 to 16.60 percent previously.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners were net buyers of 304.83 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying 625.66 million rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative turnover on the bond market on Monday was 8.9 billion rand compared with 6.10 billion rand on Monday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
